findings.title: Verified freshness is structurally but not cryptographically verified
attack_path: A producer supplies source type, source id, observation time, and an evidence label.
Retrieval treats it as usable until its deadline.
evidence: Verified requires all structural evidence fields.
No source adapter authenticates the evidence reference.
findings.recommendation: Bind high-impact freshness to authenticated adapter receipts in a later governed feature.

findings.title: Refresh-required stale facts are excluded from current context
attack_path: A volatile record reaches its half-life or has unknown freshness.
It remains a candidate for focused search.
evidence: Focused retrieval tests assert rejection and explanation.
No automatic refresh or authority escalation follows.
findings.recommendation: Preserve inspectable rejection without injecting stale content.

findings.title: Cache entries cannot outlive refresh deadlines
attack_path: A record is fresh when cached.
Its half-life elapses before the caller TTL.
Cache expiry is capped at the earlier freshness deadline.
evidence: Retrieval computes observation-plus-half-life deadlines for refresh-gated candidates.
findings.recommendation: Keep freshness transitions in cache authorization.

findings.title: Freshness metadata cannot trigger network or mutation authority
attack_path: A record is rejected as refresh required.
No tool, network, shell, provider, or memory-write call is available from the assessor.
evidence: The engine is deterministic and read-only.
Refresh requires a separately authorized workflow.
findings.recommendation: Review any future automatic refresh as a new security boundary.

limitations: Evidence references are not authenticated attestations.
Expected half-life is an operator policy rather than a guarantee.
No external source was refreshed during this review.
